sanskrit: evam ukto hanumatā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ taṃ maṇiṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā praruroda salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, Rāma, son of Daśaratha, pressing that jewel to his heart, wept together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ rāghavaḥ śokakarśitaḥ netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyāṃ sugrīvam idam abravīt
english: Beholding that finest of jewels, Rāghava, wasted by grief, his two eyes brimming with tears, spoke these words to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: yathaiva dhenuḥ sravati snehād vatsasya vatsalā tathā mamāpi hṛdayaṃ maṇiratnasya darśanāt
english: Just as a tender cow flows with milk out of love for her calf, so too my heart melts at the sight of this precious jewel.

sanskrit: maṇiratnam idaṃ dattaṃ vaidehyāḥ śvaśureṇa me vadhūkāle yathā baddham adhikaṃ mūrdhni śobhate
english: This precious jewel was given to Vaidehī by my father-in-law; fastened as it was at the time of her wedding, it shines most beautifully upon her head.

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi jalasaṃbhūto maṇiḥ pravarapūjitaḥ yajñe paramatuṣṭena dattaḥ śakreṇa dhīmatā
english: This jewel, born of water, is honored by the greatest; it was given by the wise Śakra, greatly pleased, at a sacrifice.

sanskrit: imaṃ dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ tathā tātasya darśanam adyāsmy avagataḥ saumya vaidehasya tathā vibhoḥ
english: Beholding this finest of jewels, O gentle one, today I understand it as the very sight of my father, and likewise of the great king of Videha.

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi śobhate tasyāḥ priyāyā mūrdhni me maṇiḥ adyāsya darśanenāhaṃ prāptāṃ tām iva cintaye
english: This jewel gleams upon the head of my beloved; today, by the sight of it, I imagine her as if she were present before me.

sanskrit: kim āha sītā vaidehī brūhi saumya punaḥ punaḥ parāsum iva toyena siñcantī vākyavāriṇā
english: What did Sītā, the daughter of Videha, say? Tell me again and again, O gentle one—reviving me as if with water, one nearly dead, with the water of her words.

sanskrit: itas tu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yad imaṃ vārisaṃbhavam maṇiṃ paśyāmi saumitre vaidehīm āgataṃ vinā
english: What grief could be greater than this—that I behold this jewel born of water, O son of Sumitrā, without Vaidehī having come with it?

sanskrit: ciraṃ jīvati vaidehī yadi māsaṃ dhariṣyati kṣaṇaṃ saumya na jīveyaṃ vinā tām asitekṣaṇām
english: Vaidehī will survive—if she can endure for a month; but I, O gentle one, could not live for even a moment without her, she of the dark eyes.

sanskrit: naya mām api taṃ deśaṃ yatra dṛṣṭā mama priyā na tiṣṭheyaṃ kṣaṇam api pravṛttim upalabhya ca
english: Take me also to that place where my beloved was seen; having learned of her condition, I could not remain even for a moment.

sanskrit: kathaṃ sā mama suśroṇi bhīru bhīruḥ satī tadā bhayāvahānāṃ ghorāṇāṃ madhye tiṣṭhati rakṣasām
english: How does she, my fair-hipped one, the timid, the ever-faithful one, dwell amid the fearsome and terrible rākṣasas who inspire dread?

sanskrit: śāradas timironmukho nūnaṃ candra ivāmbudaiḥ āvṛtaṃ vadanaṃ tasyā na virājati rākṣasaiḥ
english: Surely her face, shrouded by those rākṣasas, no longer shines—like the autumnal moon whose face is veiled by clouds.

sanskrit: kim āha sītā hanumaṃs tattvataḥ kathayasva me etena khalu jīviṣye bheṣajenāturo yathā
english: What did Sītā say, O Hanūmān? Tell me truthfully—by this I shall live, as a sick man lives by medicine.

sanskrit: madhurā madhurālāpā kim āha mama bhāminī madvihīnā varārohā hanuman kathayasva me duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ prāpya kathaṃ jīvati jānakī
english: The sweet one, sweet of speech—what did my passionate one say, she of noble hips, separated from me? Tell me, O Hanūmān: having attained sorrow upon sorrow, how does Jānakī live?

sanskrit: evam uktas tu hanumān rāghaveṇa mahātmanā sītāyā bhāṣitaṃ sarvaṃ nyavedayata rāghave
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Rāghava, Hanūmān reported to Rāghava everything that Sītā had spoken.

sanskrit: idam uktavatī devī jānakī puruṣarṣabha pūrvavṛttam abhijñānaṃ citrakūṭe yathā tatham
english: "This is what the goddess Jānakī said, O bull among men: she gave a token from former events at Citrakūṭa, exactly as they happened."

sanskrit: sukhasuptā tvayā sārdhaṃ jānakī pūrvam utthitā vāyasaḥ sahasotpatya virarāda stanāntare
english: "Jānakī, having slept pleasantly at your side, awoke before you; a crow suddenly flew up and cried out, pecking between her breasts."

sanskrit: paryāyeṇa ca suptas tvaṃ devyaṅke bharatāgraja punaś ca kila pakṣī sa devyā janayati vyathām
english: "Then you slept in turn in the goddess's lap, O elder brother of Bharata; and again that bird caused pain to the goddess."

sanskrit: tataḥ punar upāgamya virarāda bhṛśaṃ kila tatas tvaṃ bodhitas tasyāḥ śoṇitena samukṣitaḥ
english: "Then coming again it cried out fiercely; thereupon you were awakened, drenched with her blood."

sanskrit: vāyasena ca tenaiva satataṃ bādhyamānayā bodhitaḥ kila devyās tvaṃ sukhasuptaḥ paraṃtapa
english: "Awakened by that very crow which had been tormenting the goddess without ceasing, you, O scorcher of foes, had been sleeping peacefully."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mahābāho rāditāṃ ca stanāntare āśīviṣa iva kruddho niḥśvasann abhyabhāṣathāḥ
english: "Seeing her weeping with wounds between her breasts, O mighty-armed one, you breathed heavily like an angry serpent and addressed her."

sanskrit: nakhāgraiḥ kena te bhīru dāritaṃ tu stanāntaram kaḥ krīḍati saroṣeṇa pañcavaktreṇa bhoginā
english: "'Who, O timid one, has torn the space between your breasts with nail-tips? Who plays with an enraged five-headed serpent?'"

sanskrit: nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā vāyasaṃ samavaikṣatāḥ nakhaiḥ sarudhirais tīkṣṇair mām evābhimukhaḥ sthitam
english: "Looking around suddenly, you saw the crow—standing before you with sharp blood-stained talons—facing you directly."

sanskrit: sutaḥ kila sa śakrasya vāyasaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ dharāntaracaraḥ śīghraṃ pavanasya gatau samaḥ
english: "That crow was reportedly the son of Śakra, best among birds, roaming between earth and sky, swift as the wind in its flight."

sanskrit: tatas tasmin mahābāho kopasaṃvartitekṣaṇaḥ vāyase tvaṃ kṛtvāḥ krūrāṃ matiṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: "Then, O mighty-armed one, O best among the wise, your eyes rolling in anger, you resolved upon a cruel intention against that crow."

sanskrit: sa darbhaṃ saṃstarād gṛhya brahmāstreṇa nyayojayaḥ sa dīpta iva kālāgnir jajvālābhimukhaḥ khagam
english: "Taking a blade of darbha grass from the spread mat, you charged it with the Brahmāstra; blazing like the fire of dissolution, it flamed toward the bird."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ pradīptaṃ cikṣepa darbhaṃ taṃ vāyasaṃ prati tatas tu vāyasaṃ dīptaḥ sa darbho 'nujagāma ha
english: "You hurled that blazing blade of grass at the crow; and then that blazing grass indeed pursued the crow."

sanskrit: sa pitrā ca parityaktaḥ suraiḥ sarvair maharṣibhiḥ trīṃl lokān saṃparikramya trātāraṃ nādhigacchati
english: "Abandoned by his father, by all the gods, and by the great sages, he wandered through the three worlds and found no protector."

sanskrit: taṃ tvaṃ nipatitaṃ bhūmau śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam vadhārham api kākutstha kṛpayā paripālayaḥ
english: "Him fallen to the ground, O Kākutstha, refuge of the refuge-seeking, though deserving of death, you protected out of compassion."

sanskrit: mogham astraṃ na śakyaṃ tu kartum ity eva rāghava tatas tasyākṣikākasya hinasti sma sa dakṣiṇam
english: "The weapon could not be made to go in vain, O Rāghava—thus it destroyed the right eye of that eye-plucking crow."

sanskrit: rāma tvāṃ sa namaskṛtvā rājño daśarathasya ca visṛṣṭas tu tadā kākaḥ pratipede kham ālayam
english: "Bowing to you, O Rāma, and to king Daśaratha, that crow was then released and returned to the sky as his home."

sanskrit: evam astravidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sattvavāñ śīlavān api kimartham astraṃ rakṣaḥsu na yojayasi rāghava
english: "You who are the foremost among those who know weapons, possessed of valor, possessed of good character—why do you not employ your weapons against the rākṣasas, O Rāghava?"

sanskrit: na nāgā nāpi gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ tava rāma mukhe sthātuṃ śaktāḥ pratisamādhitum
english: "Neither nāgas, nor gandharvas, nor asuras, nor the host of Maruts are capable of standing before you in battle, O Rāma, and withstanding you."

sanskrit: tava vīryavataḥ kaccin mayi yady asti saṃbhramaḥ kṣipraṃ suniśitair bāṇair hanyatāṃ yudhi rāvaṇaḥ
english: "If you, so mighty, have any concern for me, then let Rāvaṇa be slain swiftly in battle with your well-sharpened arrows."

sanskrit: bhrātur ādeśam ādāya lakṣmaṇo vā paraṃtapaḥ sa kimarthaṃ naravaro na māṃ rakṣati rāghavaḥ
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa, the scorcher of foes, acting under his brother's command—why does he, that best of men, that Rāghava, not protect me?"

sanskrit: śaktau tau puruṣavyāghrau vāyvagnisamatejasau surāṇām api durdharṣau kimarthaṃ mām upekṣataḥ
english: "Those two tigers among men, equal in splendor to wind and fire, unconquerable even by the gods—why do they disregard me?"

sanskrit: mamaiva duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cin mahad asti na saṃśayaḥ samarthau sahitau yan māṃ nāpekṣete paraṃtapau
english: "Surely some great sin of mine exists—there is no doubt—since those two scorchers of foes, capable and united, do not regard me."

sanskrit: vaidehyā vacanaṃ śrutvā karuṇaṃ sāśrubhāṣitam punar apy aham āryāṃ tām idaṃ vacanam abruvam
english: "Having heard that pitiful, tear-choked speech of Vaidehī, I again spoke these words to that noble lady."

sanskrit: tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape rāme duḥkhābhibhūte ca lakṣmaṇaḥ paritapyate
english: "'Rāma is free of grief for you, O goddess—I swear this to you by truth; and when Rāma is overwhelmed by sorrow, Lakṣmaṇa also burns with pain.'"

sanskrit: kathaṃ cid bhavatī dṛṣṭā na kālaḥ pariśocitum imaṃ muhūrtaṃ duḥkhānām antaṃ drakṣyasi bhāmini
english: "'You have somehow been found—it is not the time for grieving; this very moment you shall see the end of your sorrows, O passionate one.'"

sanskrit: tāv ubhau naraśārdūlau rājaputrāv ariṃdamau tvaddarśanakṛtotsāhau laṅkāṃ bhasmīkariṣyataḥ
english: "'Those two tigers among men, princes, destroyers of enemies, roused to eagerness by the prospect of seeing you, will reduce Laṅkā to ashes.'"

sanskrit: hatvā ca samare raudraṃ rāvaṇaṃ saha bāndhavam rāghavas tvāṃ mahābāhuḥ svāṃ purīṃ nayate dhruvam
english: "'And having slain the terrible Rāvaṇa along with his kin in battle, the mighty-armed Rāghava will certainly lead you back to his own city.'"

sanskrit: yat tu rāmo vijānīyād abhijñānam anindite prītisaṃjananaṃ tasya pradātuṃ tattvam arhasi
english: "'Whatever token might let Rāma know—something that will generate delight in him, O blameless one—you should truly give it.'"

sanskrit: sābhivīkṣya diśaḥ sarvā veṇyudgrathanam uttamam muktvā vastrād dadau mahyaṃ maṇim etaṃ mahābala
english: "She, gazing in all directions, loosened the excellent binding of her braid and, from her garment, gave me this jewel, O mighty one."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya maṇiṃ divyaṃ tava heto raghūttama śirasā saṃpraṇamyainām aham āgamane tvare
english: "Receiving that divine jewel for your sake, O best of the Raghus, bowing to her with my head, I hastened in my coming."

sanskrit: gamane ca kṛtotsāham avekṣya varavarṇinī vivardhamānaṃ ca hi mām uvāca janakātmajā aśrupūrṇamukhī dīnā bāṣpasaṃdigdhabhāṣiṇī
english: "And seeing me roused to eagerness for departure and growing in size, the daughter of Janaka, that fair-complexioned one, her face filled with tears, pitiful, her words choked with weeping, spoke to me."

sanskrit: hanuman siṃhasaṃkāśau tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ sarvān brūyā anāmayam
english: "'O Hanūmān, convey my greeting of freedom from ill to both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who are like lions, and to Sugrīva together with his ministers, to all of them.'"

sanskrit: yathā ca sa mahābāhur māṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ asmād duḥkhāmbusaṃrodhāt tat samādhātum arhasi
english: "'And you should endeavor to arrange how that mighty-armed Rāghava may rescue me from this flood of sorrow that hems me in.'"

sanskrit: imaṃ ca tīvraṃ mama śokavegaṃ rakṣobhir ebhiḥ paribhartsanaṃ ca brūyās tu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṃ śivaś ca te 'dhvāstu haripravīra
english: "'And when you reach Rāma's presence, tell him of this fierce surge of my grief and of the taunts of these rākṣasas. May your journey be auspicious, O hero among monkeys.'"

sanskrit: etat tavāryā nṛparājasiṃha sītā vacaḥ prāha viṣādapūrvam etac ca buddhvā gaditaṃ mayā tvaṃ śraddhatsva sītāṃ kuśalāṃ samagrām
english: "This is the speech that your noble Sītā spoke to you, O lion among kings of kings, full of despondency. Understanding this, I have told you—believe that Sītā is well and whole."

sanskrit: athāham uttaraṃ devyā punar uktaḥ sasaṃbhramam tava snehān naravyāghra sauhāryād anumānya ca
english: "Then I was again addressed urgently by the goddess with a further message: 'Out of love for you, O tiger among men, and having obtained your friendship—'

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vācyo rāmo dāśarathis tvayā yathā mām āpnuyāc chīghraṃ hatvā rāvaṇam āhave
english: "'—you must speak to Rāma, son of Daśaratha, in many such ways, so that he may quickly recover me, having slain Rāvaṇa in battle.'"

sanskrit: yadi vā manyase vīra vasaikāham ariṃdama kasmiṃś cit saṃvṛte deśe viśrāntaḥ śvo gamiṣyasi
english: "'Or if you think it fit, O hero, O subduer of enemies, stay one day in some hidden place; rested, you shall depart tomorrow.'"

sanskrit: mama cāpy alpabhāgyāyāḥ sāmnidhyāt tava vānara asya śokavipākasya muhūrtaṃ syād vimokṣaṇam
english: "'And by your nearness to me, O monkey—I who am so bereft of good fortune—there might be for a moment a release from the full ripening of this grief.'"

sanskrit: gate hi tvayi vikrānte punarāgamanāya vai prāṇānām api saṃdeho mama syān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "'For once you, the mighty, have departed with regard to returning, even my very survival will be in doubt—of this there is no uncertainty.'"

sanskrit: tavādarśanajaḥ śoko bhūyo māṃ paritāpayet duḥkhād duḥkhaparābhūtāṃ durgatāṃ duḥkhabhāginīm
english: "'The grief born of not seeing you would torment me further—me, overcome by sorrow upon sorrow, fallen low, a sharer in misery.'"

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu vīrasaṃdehas tiṣṭhatīva mamāgrataḥ sumahāṃs tvatsahāyeṣu haryṛkṣeṣu asaṃśayaḥ
english: "'Yet this great doubt about your heroes stands as it were before me—a very great doubt, without question, concerning your allies, the monkeys and bears.'"

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu khalu duṣpāraṃ tariṣyanti mahodadhim tāni haryṛkṣasainyāni tau vā naravarātmajau
english: "'How will those armies of monkeys and bears cross the great ocean, so difficult to cross? Or how will those two sons of the best of men?'"

sanskrit: trayāṇām eva bhūtānāṃ sāgarasyāsya laṅghane śaktiḥ syād vainateyasya vāyor vā tava vānagha
english: "'The power to leap over this ocean would belong to only three beings: Vainateya, or Vāyu, or you, O blameless monkey.'"

sanskrit: tad asmin kāryaniyoge vīraivaṃ duratikrame kiṃ paśyasi samādhānaṃ brūhi kāryavidāṃ vara
english: "'So in this undertaking of heroes, so difficult to accomplish, what solution do you see? Tell me, O best among those who know what must be done.'"

sanskrit: kāmam asya tvam evaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane paryāptaḥ paravīraghna yaśasyas te balodayaḥ
english: "'Granted, you alone are sufficient for the accomplishment of this task, O slayer of enemy heroes; your rise of power brings you glory.'"

sanskrit: balaiḥ samagrair yadi māṃ hatvā rāvaṇam āhave vijayī svāṃ purīṃ rāmo nayet tat syād yaśaskaram
english: "'But if Rāma, victorious, were to lead me to his own city with his full forces, having slain Rāvaṇa in battle—that would bring him glory.'"

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ tasya vīrasya vanād upadhinā hṛtā rakṣasā tad bhayād eva tathā nārhati rāghavaḥ
english: "'Just as I was carried off from the forest by that rākṣasa through guile, Rāghava should not act out of that same fear alone—that would not befit him.'"

sanskrit: balais tu saṃkulāṃ kṛtvā laṅkāṃ parabalārdanaḥ māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthas tat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet
english: "'But if Kākutstha, the crusher of enemy armies, were to overrun Laṅkā with his forces and then lead me away—that would be worthy of him.'"

sanskrit: tad yathā tasya vikrāntam anurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ bhavaty āhavaśūrasya tathā tvam upapādaya
english: "'So arrange it in such a way that it may be fitting for that great-souled one's heroism, fitting for the valor of that hero in battle.'"

sanskrit: tad arthopahitaṃ vākyaṃ praśritaṃ hetusaṃhitam niśamyāhaṃ tataḥ śeṣaṃ vākyam uttaram abruvam
english: "Having heard that speech, laden with meaning, humble, joined with reasoning, I then spoke the following further words in reply."

sanskrit: devi haryṛkṣasainyānām īśvaraḥ plavatāṃ varaḥ sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṃpannas tavārthe kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: "'O goddess, Sugrīva, lord of the armies of monkeys and bears, best among the leapers, endowed with valor, is firmly resolved for your sake.'"

sanskrit: tasya vikramasaṃpannāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ manaḥsaṃkalpasaṃpātā nideśe harayaḥ sthitāḥ
english: "'The monkeys who stand under his command are endowed with heroism, possessed of valor, of great strength, swift as the speed of the mind's resolve.'"

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ nopari nādhastān na tiryak sajjate gatiḥ na ca karmasu sīdanti mahatsv amitatejasaḥ
english: "'Their movement is unimpeded above, below, or sideways; and they do not falter in great deeds—those of immeasurable splendor.'"

sanskrit: asakṛt tair mahābhāgair vānarair balasaṃyutaiḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtā bhūmir vāyumārgānusāribhiḥ
english: "'Not once but many times have those greatly fortunate, powerful monkeys, who travel the path of the wind, circumambulated the earth.'"

sanskrit: madviśiṣṭāś ca tulyāś ca santi tatra vanaukasaḥ mattaḥ pratyavaraḥ kaś cin nāsti sugrīvasaṃnidhau
english: "'There are forest-dwellers there who are both superior to me and equal to me; none in Sugrīva's company is inferior to me.'"

sanskrit: ahaṃ tāvad iha prāptaḥ kiṃ punas te mahābalāḥ na hi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ
english: "'I, at least, have reached here—how much more so those of great power? For it is not the foremost who are sent on missions; it is the lesser folk who are sent.'"

sanskrit: tad alaṃ paritāpena devi manyur vyapaitu te ekotpātena te laṅkām eṣyanti hariyūthapāḥ
english: "'Therefore, enough of anguish, O goddess; let your anger depart. The leaders of monkey troops will come to Laṅkā in a single leap.'"

sanskrit: mama pṛṣṭhagatau tau ca candrasūryāv ivoditau tvatsakāśaṃ mahābhāge nṛsiṃhāv āgamiṣyataḥ
english: "'And those two—like the risen sun and moon—mounted upon my back, those two lion-men will come into your presence, O greatly fortunate one.'"

sanskrit: arighnaṃ siṃhasaṃkāśaṃ kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi rāghavam lakṣmaṇaṃ ca dhanuṣpāṇiṃ laṅkā dvāram upasthitam
english: "'You will swiftly see Rāghava, the slayer of enemies, like a lion, and Lakṣmaṇa with bow in hand, standing at the gates of Laṅkā.'"

sanskrit: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhān vīrān siṃhaśārdūlavikramān vānarān vānarendrābhān kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi saṃgatān
english: "'You will swiftly see the heroes assembled—armed with nails and fangs, with the stride of lions and tigers, those monkeys resembling lords of monkeys.'"

sanskrit: śailāmbudan nikāśānāṃ laṅkāmalayasānuṣu nardatāṃ kapimukhyānām acirāc choṣyase svanam
english: "'You will soon hear the roar of the chiefs of monkeys, resembling mountains and storm-clouds, roaring upon the slopes of Laṅkā's Malaya hills.'"

sanskrit: nivṛttavanavāsaṃ ca tvayā sārdham ariṃdamam abhiṣiktam ayodhyāyāṃ kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi rāghavam
english: "'And you will swiftly see Rāghava—his forest exile over, the subduer of enemies—consecrated as king at Ayodhyā, together with you.'"

sanskrit: tato mayā vāgbhir adīnabhāṣiṇī śivābhir iṣṭābhir abhiprasāditā jagāma śāntiṃ mama maithilātmajā tavāpi śokena tathābhipīḍitā
english: "Then, consoled by me with auspicious and pleasing words spoken without despondency, the daughter of the king of Mithilā attained peace—she too, so afflicted by grief on your account."
